If you have a roommate with it, she might borrow your clothes. You get mad, tell her not to do it again (because she spilled grape juice[red wine] on your beautiful white dress!), and she agrees, saying she's sorry. Could children one day sue parents for posting baby pics on Facebook?
This is why France has strict privacy laws. "French parents 'could be jailed' for posting children’s photos online" https://archive.is/POlJD

Yes and no.

1) the new generations are grown up getting used to share pretty much everything online, with everyone, strangers included. They see it as a natural thing to do, not a violation of their privacy, so it would be surprising if they decided that their parents violated their privacy somehow by doing exactly the same thing. This could be different if the pictures taken are, somehow, humiliating to them, and this might be a very subjective matter.

2) babies and little kids (but even teens) physical characteristics change very fast while growing up. So it would be quite hard to link the kid in an old picture with an adult. So, even if your parents shared a picture of yourself that you don't like for whatever reason... that happened a long time ago making it irrelevant and you changed enough to become unrecognizable anyways.

IMO it is much more likely that the kids that do "stupid things" today on YouTube will feel humiliated by their own videos in a decade or so. By that time they will probably have lost the passwords of their old accounts and be unable to delete anything. Everyone does stupid things when little, i did loads of stupid things, but today's kids will have those stupid moments come back haunting them forever. On the good side... they will not be alone. This will be a problem so widespread that it will probably become just a fact of life like... "yeah... when i was a kid i did shit my pants... but so did you, so what"?

I would see it as more problematic the practice of "annotating" the pictures with their personal data... that is way more likely to cause problems in future since search engines are very good at scanning text and storing it forever and it is something that i hate too. You certainly don't want the first link that comes up on Google while searching for your name to be the picture when, at 4, you pissed yourself in your pants in school in front of everyone. So, if you have to share some pictures of your kids, just avoid to annotate them and avoid sharing pictures that can be humiliating to them.
